title: Martin's cloak (c. 316–397)
hookLine: a soldier cuts his cloak in half for a beggar and dreams of Christ wearing it

cards: A winter so cold, Sulpicius says, that people were dying of it. A young soldier named Martin rides up to the gate of the city of Amiens.
At the gate stands a man with no clothes at all, asking the people going in and out for help. They pass him. Martin has already given away what else he had.
All that's left is the cloak on his back and the sword at his side. And he looks at the cloak, and then at the sword.

teach.h: HALF THE CLOAK, CUT WITH A SWORD.
teach.b: The story comes from Sulpicius Severus, who wrote a life of Martin and says he knew him. Martin draws his sword, cuts the cloak in two, gives one half to the man, and wraps himself in what's left. Notice the half.
He doesn't hand over the whole thing and ride off a hero. He shares it, and goes on looking a little ridiculous. Sulpicius says some of the bystanders laughed at how he looked.
Others were ashamed, because they had more to give and hadn't given it. Then the night.
Martin is asleep, and in a dream he sees Christ, wearing the half of the cloak he gave away. He's told to look closely and recognize it.

And he hears Christ say to the angels around him, more or less: Martin, who is still only a catechumen, clothed me with this. A catechumen is someone still preparing for baptism. Martin wasn't even baptized yet.
Sulpicius ties the dream to words of Jesus in Matthew. In the Douay-Rheims: "as long as you did it to one of these my least brethren, you did it to me."
Martin, Sulpicius says, didn't grow proud over the dream. He took it as a push, and went to be baptized.

So the story has two halves, like the cloak: a man at a gate, and Christ in the dream, wearing the same piece of cloth. The Catholic Church remembers Martin as a saint, a soldier who later became a monk and a bishop.

how: Catholics honor Martin of Tours as a saint; in parts of Europe his feast is kept with lantern processions and shared food, and some parishes run coat and blanket drives as winter begins.

games.q: you're Martin at the city gate in winter. a man with no clothes asks for help. you have a cloak and a sword. what do you do?
o: ride on; others will help him.
cut the cloak in two and give him half.
give him the whole cloak and freeze.
games.why: he cut it in half and kept the rest, looking odd enough that some people laughed. that night he saw Christ wearing the half.

practice: Start with the cold, not the closet: where near you is someone likely to be outside tonight, a bus stop, a doorway, the steps of a church?
Let one place come clear, and ask what warm thing could reach it, a coat, a blanket, a scarf, or the price of one, by way of a shelter, a coat drive or a parish collection.
If you pray, remember that person by name, or by the place they stand.

wordCard.voice: Martin's cloak. Half a soldier's cloak, cut with his sword for a freezing man, and worn by Christ in Martin's dream. Today's word.
